cultural.vision_reason: This is a Company School costume-album watercolour, captioned "Malay Waders," showing a couple in leaf skirts with bow, arrow and boomerang-like club — attire and equipment typical of hunter-gatherer forest/coastal peoples (e.g. Andamanese/aboriginal groups) rather than the sarong-and-keris dress culture of the Malay people proper, and the album itself is titled "costumes of South India," suggesting a mismatched or mislabeled ethnic attribution.

physical.title: painting; album
physical.summary: Page from an album of sketches of costumes of South India (opaque watercolour with letterpress). Company School, on European paper watermarked Moreley & Saunders 1842 depicting Malay Waders. The couple are both dressed in leaf skirts. The man carries in his left hand a bow, in his right an arrow, and a knife is stuck in his belt. The woman leans on what appears to be a club or a boomerang. From her waistband emerge the handles of what could possibly be a catapult.

cultural.vision_reason: This Company School watercolour depicts a South Indian hill tribe ("Malay Abassens," likely a Malayali/Malabar hill people) hunting with bow and arrow, not the Malaysian Malay ethnic group despite the superficial name overlap — the metadata explicitly places it in South India.

physical.title: painting; album
physical.summary: Page from an album of sketches of costumes of South India (opaque watercolour with letterpress). Company School, on European paper watermarked Moreley & Saunders 1842 depicting Malay Abassens (?). The figure on the left, with a gaunt face, dressed in a loincloth and with the hair tied in a topknot, has a bow and a quiver slung over his shoulder. In his right hand he carries his prey. The figure to the right, with a fuller face, wears the same dress and hairstyle. In the left hand he has an arrow, and from his right arm hangs a container. The background suggests a mountainous region. This is the only page of the album that depicts two male figures, instead of a man and a woman.
